symbol_dictionary: allSectors is the entire finite list of noncentral sectors, including any multiplicities, fixed before the level tends to infinity. sector is the coherent polynomial contribution of one whole sector.
whole and central lie in a commutative coefficient ring A; fill maps A to a commutative ring B and is explicitly assumed additive and zero-preserving. No multiplication preservation is used.
hypotheses: whole=central+sectorSum allSectors sector; fill(0)=0 and fill(x+y)=fill(x)+fill(y).
relations.conclusion: fill(whole)−fill(central) equals the coherent sum of the filled sectors.
relations.notes: The equality formalizes the additive assembly step only. A particular diagram must supply the complete list and its decomposition; matrix operators at different boxes are not identified with commuting elements.

total is the ordinary finite sum. No entropy, convex function, minimizer, diagram or asymptotic rate is defined by this scalar module.
polynomialSize is the supplied polynomial norm and absoluteValue is the supplied filled-value magnitude; they are arbitrary maps with the explicitly stated bounds, not a constructed Hermitian form.
degreeAdmissible records the separately bounded spectral degree at every box. operatorBound is required only on this admissible class, not on arbitrary higher-degree polynomials.
operatorCost is the nonnegative product filling cost, weights are the sector prefactors, and envelope is their shared exponential bound.
hypotheses: The coherent full decomposition and additivity hypotheses hold; absoluteValue is zero at zero and subadditive.
Every listed sector is degreeAdmissible. Its filled magnitude is bounded by operatorCost times polynomialSize, and its polynomialSize is bounded by weights(index) times envelope.
operatorCost≥0.
relations.conclusion: The magnitude of fill(whole)−fill(central) is at most operatorCost·(sum sector weights)·envelope.
unformalized: The actual sector decomposition, admissibility proof, full-source norm estimates, polynomial filling cost and their geometric calibration.
relations.notes: The source is assembled coherently before the magnitude triangle inequality. The theorem neither replaces a Gram matrix by the identity nor infers a lower bound on the marked closing coefficient.

symbol_dictionary: allSectors is a fixed finite list, individualThreshold gives a natural cutoff for each list member, and sectorThreshold is their list maximum.
levelScope is any retained predicate on levels, such as all levels N≥3 or the prescribed parity; estimate is an arbitrary sector-and-level proposition.
hypotheses: For each member, the estimate holds at every level above its individual threshold that also satisfies levelScope.
relations.conclusion: Above sectorThreshold the estimates hold simultaneously for every listed sector, with the original levelScope unchanged.
relations.notes: This is the finite logical step after the individual estimates. It does not prove their analytic content and does not replace an all-level claim by a subsequence.
